env.docs: Bind port. Read by the Dioxus toolchain, not by this loader.
env.name: PORT

env.docs: Bind address. Read by the Dioxus toolchain, not by this loader.
env.name: IP

dist_dir.description:
Directory holding the `dx bundle` output, relative to the working directory.

The image runs from `/app`, next to `public/`, so the default resolves without anything
being set.

script_nonce.description:
Whether `script-src` reserves a per-response nonce for the script Cloudflare injects at the
edge.

On by default, because this site is delivered through a Cloudflare Tunnel with the bot
products active; the `__cf_bm` and `cf_clearance` cookies are theirs. Those products inject
an inline `<script>` after the HTML leaves this process, so no hash the server computes can
cover it, and without the nonce the detection silently never runs. Cloudflare reads the
nonce from the `Content-Security-Policy` response header and copies it onto what it
injects.

The server sends `Cache-Control: no-cache` on every document, so a cache must revalidate a
stored copy with this origin before each reuse. A document carries no validator, so every
reuse reaches the server, which mints a fresh nonce per response. **No Cloudflare Cache
Rule may cache the documents**: a "Cache Everything" rule overrides that header at the
edge, and nothing inside this process can see it.

turnstile.description:
Whether `script-src` and `frame-src` admit `https://challenges.cloudflare.com`, for a
Turnstile widget.

Off, because this site has no form behind a challenge. A managed-challenge interstitial
needs nothing here: it is a Cloudflare-served document carrying its own policy.

web_analytics.description:
Whether the policy admits the Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon and the endpoint it reports
to.

Off, because this site measures nothing, which the privacy page states. It covers the
manual snippet only; the automatic edge injection is an inline script and needs
`script_nonce`.

hash_inline_scripts.description:
Whether the server admits inline `<script>` by hash, in place of `'unsafe-inline'`.

On, the default, the server hashes the response body it is about to send, so the only
inline scripts that run are the ones it rendered. `'unsafe-inline'` admits an injected
`<script>` as readily as the Dioxus hydration bootstrap.

Off restores `'unsafe-inline'` with a restart. Use it when the browser refuses an inline
script the scanner does not see, which shows as a blank page and a console message. Known
cases are a development server that injects a live-reload script downstream of this
process, and a renderer change that emits script this server never sees.

A policy carrying any hash or nonce makes `'unsafe-inline'` inert, so turning this off also
requires `csp.cloudflare.script_nonce = false`. [`validate`](Self::validate) refuses the
boot otherwise.

include_subdomains.description: Whether the policy covers every subdomain as well, as `includeSubDomains`.

max_age_secs.description:
How long, in seconds, a browser keeps to HTTPS after seeing the header. Zero clears it.

Zero is the documented way to withdraw HSTS: a browser drops a host it learned from this
header on the next response. A host already on the preload list stays there until its
removal reaches browsers in a release. Zero is refused together with `preload`, which it
would contradict.

preload.description:
Whether the header asks for the host to be included in the browsers' built-in HSTS preload
list, as `preload`.

The boot enforces the list's own requirements: `include_subdomains` on and a
`max_age_secs` of at least one year.

cache_dir.description:
The writable directory rendered HTML is cached into. Unset or empty disables ISR.

Keep it outside the bundled `public/` asset tree so those content-hashed assets stay
immutable. The image points it at a sub-directory of `/tmp`, which the deployment provides
as a writable mount even under a read-only root filesystem.

Default: ISR off; the image sets `/tmp/isr`.

ttl_secs.description:
The revalidation interval in seconds. Zero means a permanent cache.

A page changes only with a new build or a new `legal.*` configuration, and the server keeps
whatever the directory holds at boot. Permanent suits a directory that starts empty with
every pod. A container restart inside the same pod keeps the mount and its pages, so a
`legal.*` change applied by a restart needs a positive value, a cleared directory or a new
pod. A cache volume that outlives a deploy needs a positive value for the same reason.

Default: permanent.

default_locale.description:
Locale served when neither the request nor its `Accept-Language` header matches a
published one, for example `en`. Without it, the first published locale in alphabetical
order is served.

body.description:
Markdown text per locale, keyed by locale (`en`, `de-AT`). Usually supplied through a
`…__BODY__<LOCALE>_FILE` variable naming a mounted file. Each text is at most 1 MiB.
Exclusive with `url`.

order.description: Position in the index, lowest first. Documents with the same value are ordered by slug.

title.description: Display title per locale, keyed like `body`.

url.description:
Absolute `http` or `https` URL of a document hosted elsewhere, without credentials.
Exclusive with `body`.

documents.description:
The published documents, keyed by the slug their URL uses. A slug is lowercase letters,
digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters, and starts with a letter or a digit.

attach_stacktraces.description: Whether events that carry no stack trace of their own get one attached.

breadcrumb_level.description:
The least severe `tracing` level kept as a breadcrumb, the trail attached to the next
issue.

Records at or above `sentry.capture_level` become issues instead, so the two thresholds
partition the stream.

capture_level.description: The least severe `tracing` level reported as a Sentry issue.

debug.description: Whether the SDK prints its own diagnostics to stderr, for proving a DSN works.

dsn.description:
The ingest URL, `https://<key>@<host>/<project>`.

The embedded key is a bearer credential for the project's ingest endpoint. Supply it as
`PORTFOLIO_SENTRY__DSN_FILE=/run/secrets/sentry_dsn`, or as `sentry__dsn` inside
`$PORTFOLIO_SECRETS_DIR`, so it never enters the process environment, where
`/proc/<pid>/environ`, a crash dump and `docker inspect` all carry it and every child
process inherits it.

Absent while `sentry.enabled` is set, it fails the boot.

enabled.description:
Whether the server initializes the Sentry client. Off installs no client, panic hook,
`tracing` layer or HTTP middleware, and nothing leaves the process.

It also decides who owns the log subscriber. Off, the Dioxus toolchain installs its own.
On, the server installs one first, still reading `RUST_LOG` and formatting the same way,
because a Sentry layer has to be a layer of the subscriber.

environment.description:
The environment tag on every event.

Unset resolves to `production` for a release build and `development` otherwise. The
workspace ships one image, so the build profile is what separates a developer's
`dx serve` from the deployed container.

Default: `production` in a release build, `development` otherwise.

http_transactions.description:
Whether the server records one Sentry transaction per request, named by the matched route.

Naming by route keeps `/api/v1/legal/{slug}` one transaction name for every document.
Whether a started transaction is kept is `sentry.traces_sample_rate`'s decision. Off starts
no transaction, but the HTTP middleware stays installed and still attaches the request to
events.

max_breadcrumbs.description: The most breadcrumbs one event carries.

release.description:
The release tag on every event.

Unset resolves to `portfolio@<version>`, the workspace version the binary was built from.
Every deploy is a new image cut from a new version, so the tag attributes a regression to
a deploy.

Default: `portfolio@` and the built version.

sample_rate.description:
The fraction of captured events sent, from `0.0` to `1.0`.

It is a blunt volume cap: a rare bug is as likely to be dropped as a noisy one. Leave it
at `1.0` unless a quota forces otherwise.

send_default_pii.description:
Whether every event carries personally identifying data: the client IP, the full request
header set including `Cookie`, and the resolved user.

**Off, and worth leaving off.** A crash report is actionable without a reader's IP address
and cookies, and every event sent is personal data handed to a third party, which the
published privacy notice would then have to name. On, it also stops the HTTP middleware
from redacting sensitive request headers.

server_name.description:
The host tag on every event. Unset reports none.

The hostname of a replica is infrastructure detail, and this site runs one image behind a
tunnel, so it identifies nothing an event does not already say.

span_attributes.description:
Whether `tracing` span fields are copied onto the Sentry span as attributes.

Off, because span fields here carry request paths and the negotiated locale, and a
transaction is stored under a longer retention than a log line.

traces_sample_rate.description:
The fraction of request traces recorded, from `0.0` to `1.0`.

The rate decides for a request that arrives without a sampling decision. A request whose
`sentry-trace` header carries one keeps it, so a caller can have its request recorded even
at the default, `0.0`. `sentry.http_transactions = false` starts no request transaction at
all. The default keeps ordinary traffic from sending performance data when Sentry is on for
crash reporting. `0.05` to `0.2` is an ordinary production figure.
